categoryName: Chronic & prescription basics a campus dispensary must hold — diabetes, BP, thyroid, asthma, antibiotics policy

skuLines.line: Metformin — plain IR and SR, 500mg / 850mg / 1g
skuLines.examples: Glycomet 500 / Glycomet SR 500 (USV), Gluconorm SR 500 (Lupin), Okamet (Cipla), Biciphage SR
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 10 / 15 / 20; bottle of 30-100 for long-term users
skuLines.priceBand: ₹13-52 per strip (Glycomet 500 10s ₹19.59 MRP; Glycomet 1g 15s ₹63.46; Gluconorm SR 500 15s ₹32.45)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round. Refill demand steps up at term start (Apr, Jul) when staff return with fresh prescriptions and dips in vacation weeks.
skuLines.marginBand: 16% fixed on the DPCO ceiling price (metformin is a scheduled NLEM molecule); ~20% on non-scheduled brand extensions
skuLines.notes: The single highest-volume chronic molecule in India and the anchor of the whole diabetes shelf. Stock in depth — never go out. Metformin sits under Schedule H (prescription-only). Shelf life 24-36 months; expiry risk near zero because it turns fast.

skuLines.line: Glimepiride ± metformin FDC (sulfonylurea combos)
skuLines.examples: Gemer 1/2/3mg + Gemer DS + Gemer P (Sun), Glycomet GP 1/2 (USV), Amaryl M (Sanofi), Gluconorm G (Lupin), Okamet GM (Cipla)
skuLines.priceBand: ₹35-260 per strip (GP 1mg 10s ₹35.14; Glycomet GP 2 15s ₹180; Gemer DS 2 15s ₹253; Gluconorm G 2 15s ₹359.75)
skuLines.marginBand: 16% on scheduled strengths; 20-22% on non-scheduled FDC extensions
skuLines.notes: Carry at least 1mg and 2mg in both plain and DS/forte. Hypoglycaemia risk means an elderly resident who skips a hill-weather meal can crash — the pharmacist should hand out glucose sachets alongside. Being pushed down to 3rd line by SGLT2/GLP-1 but still the volume seller at this price point.

skuLines.line: DPP-4 inhibitor FDCs — sitagliptin / vildagliptin / teneligliptin + metformin
skuLines.examples: Istamet 50/500 (Sun), Galvus Met 50/500 (Cipla/Novartis), Jalra M (USV), Vysov M 50/500, Dynaglipt M, Zita Met
skuLines.priceBand: ₹92-390 per strip (Istamet 50/500 15s ₹176.25; Galvus Met 15s ₹372.45; Jalra M 15s ₹326.40; Dynaglipt M 10s ₹121.16)
skuLines.marginBand: 20-22% (mostly non-scheduled brands, so full trade margin applies)
skuLines.notes: Weight-neutral and no hypoglycaemia, so specialists in Solan/Chandigarh prescribe these heavily to staff. High ticket (₹300-400/month) — this is where a chronic register pays for itself, because a single missed refill sends a resident 30-50 km to town.

skuLines.line: SGLT2 inhibitor — dapagliflozin / empagliflozin, plain and in double/triple FDC
skuLines.examples: Dapagain 10 (₹80.10/15s), Empaglyde 25 (₹90.85/10s), Gluxit Pro, Dapanorm GM (Alkem), Gemer Dapa XR 10/2/500 (Sun)
skuLines.priceBand: ₹80-330 per strip (Dapagain 10 15s ₹80.10; Gemer Dapa XR 10/2/500 7s ₹126; Dapanorm GM 10s ₹153.10; higher triples to ₹326)
skuLines.marginBand: 20-25% (non-scheduled; heavy brand competition after Indian patent expiry has widened retailer margin)
skuLines.notes: The fastest-growing oral class in India in 2025-26 and now standard 2nd line because of the kidney/heart benefit. Triple FDCs (SGLT2 + sulfonylurea + metformin) are new and a store that only stocks metformin + glimepiride will send these prescriptions away. Cheap now — dozens of Indian brands.

skuLines.line: Older oral antidiabetics — voglibose, acarbose, pioglitazone
skuLines.examples: Vogliboz 0.3 (₹100.57/10s), Volix, Pioz 15/30 (USV), Dailyvog
skuLines.notes: Low volume but a few long-standing patients will be on exactly these. Stock one strength each rather than a range; buy against the chronic register, not on spec.

skuLines.line: Oral semaglutide (GLP-1) — originator plus 2026 Indian generics
skuLines.examples: Rybelsus 3/7/14mg (Novo Nordisk), Obeda 3mg (Dr Reddy's, ₹881.10/10s), Semalix 7 (₹1,326.10/10s), Sematrinity & Noveltreat (Sun), Semaglyn (Zydus), Glipiq (Glenmark)
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 10 tablets (a 10-day starter or a titration step)
skuLines.priceBand: ₹2,250-3,628 per 10s for Rybelsus and premium brands; ₹880-1,330 per 10s for the 2026 Indian generics
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; new starts cluster after annual health checks
skuLines.marginBand: 20-25% on generics — the highest absolute rupee margin per pack on the whole shelf (₹200-300 per strip)
skuLines.notes: India's semaglutide patent expired March 2026 and 40-50 domestic brands launched; generic 3mg now runs about a quarter of Rybelsus. GLP-1s are top of every Indian e-pharmacy best-seller list in 2026. Highest-value pack a campus store will handle — stock 1-2 strengths against named patients only, and never speculate on inventory at ₹900-3,600 a strip.

skuLines.line: Human insulin — regular, NPH and 30:70 premix, vials and 3ml cartridges
skuLines.examples: Actrapid / Insulatard / Mixtard (Novo Nordisk), Huminsulin (Lilly), Lupisulin R / N / M 30:70 (Lupin), Wosulin (Wockhardt)
skuLines.packSizes: 10ml vial 40IU/100IU; box of 5 x 3ml cartridges; disposable pens
skuLines.priceBand: ₹177-182 per 10ml vial; ₹466-516 per 3ml cartridge (Lupisulin M 30/70 3ml ₹466.50; Actrapid 10ml ₹182.70)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; NEVER allow a stockout, there is no substitute source within 30-50 km
skuLines.marginBand: 16% (all insulins are scheduled/price-controlled NLEM formulations — thin margin, but it is a life-safety line, not a profit line)
skuLines.notes: COLD CHAIN, 2-8°C, non-negotiable: a lockable pharmacy fridge with a thermometer, a logged daily temperature record and power backup. In a cold hill winter FREEZING is as damaging as heat — frozen insulin must be discarded, so the fridge cannot sit against an unheated outside wall. In-use pen/vial keeps ~28 days below 30°C. Ship in a validated cold box on the hill route; do not let a carton ride an unheated truck bay in January.

skuLines.line: Insulin analogues — basal glargine and rapid-acting aspart / lispro
skuLines.examples: Lantus (Sanofi), Basalog (Biocon), Glaritus (Wockhardt), Basugine (Lupin), Novorapid / Humalog, Lupilispro
skuLines.priceBand: ₹620-652 per 3ml cartridge; ₹842 per 5ml vial; ₹2,173 per 10ml Lantus vial
skuLines.marginBand: 16-20% (glargine biosimilars carry a little more than the price-controlled human insulins)
skuLines.notes: Any type 1 child or young adult on campus is on these — a residential school with 5,000 residents will have several. Same 2-8°C cold chain and freeze risk as above. Hold ONE basal and ONE rapid brand per patient and never switch brands without the prescriber, because unit-for-unit equivalence is not assumed by patients.

skuLines.line: Pen needles and insulin syringes (U-40 / U-100)
skuLines.examples: Novofine 31G 6mm, BD Ultra-Fine Pen III 4mm 32G, Accu-Chek FastClix pen needles, BD U-40 insulin syringe
skuLines.priceBand: ₹13.86 per single Novofine needle; ₹77-101 per box of 5; ₹1,018-1,734 per box of 50-100; ₹115 per 10 syringes
skuLines.marginBand: 20-30% (device consumable, not price-controlled)
skuLines.notes: The classic stockout that ruins insulin therapy — the pen is useless without the needle, and patients re-use needles when the store is out. Match the needle to the pen the resident actually owns (Novo vs Lilly vs Biocon pens). Pair with a sharps disposal box; used needles in a campus dustbin are a real injury hazard around children.

skuLines.line: Glucometer starter kit (meter + lancing device + 10-25 strips)
skuLines.examples: Accu-Chek Instant / Active (Roche), Dr Morepen Gluco One BG-03, BPL Gluco Monitoring Device, Contour Plus, Standard Mentor
skuLines.packSizes: 1 kit per box, usually with 10 or 25 free strips
skuLines.priceBand: ₹820-3,499 MRP (Accu-Chek Instant kit ₹820-1,124; Dr Morepen with 25 strips ₹1,085; BPL kit ₹1,499; BPL 110-strip bundle ₹3,499)
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes after camp health checks and at term start
skuLines.marginBand: 25-45% — meters are often sold near cost precisely to lock in the strip annuity
skuLines.notes: Deliberately standardise on ONE OR TWO meter families for the whole campus. Every extra brand means another dead strip SKU, and strips are the item that expires. The meter is the razor; the strips are the blades.

skuLines.line: Glucometer test strips (matched to the meters actually installed on campus)
skuLines.examples: Accu-Chek Instant / Active strips 50s, Dr Morepen BG-03 strips 50s, BPL strips 25s/50s/100s, Contour Plus 50s
skuLines.notes: Highest expiry-write-off risk on the chronic shelf: strips are humidity and temperature sensitive, and once a vial is opened it is typically good only 3-6 months. Order to the register (patients x tests/week), not to a shelf plan. Batch-code lot matching matters on older meters.

skuLines.line: Lancets for finger-prick testing
skuLines.examples: Accu-Chek Softclix 25s/200s, Accusure lancets 100s, Dr Odin lancets
skuLines.notes: Cheap, long-dated, high-margin, and constantly forgotten. Must match the lancing device brand — a Softclix drum will not fit an Accusure pen.

skuLines.line: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) sensor
skuLines.examples: FreeStyle Libre / Libre 2 sensor (Abbott)
skuLines.packSizes: 1 sensor (14-day wear) per box; reader sold separately or phone-based
skuLines.marginBand: 12-20% (thin; a low-discount, brand-controlled device line)
skuLines.notes: 2026's premium diabetes line — moved from hospital to retail. Only worth holding against a named subscriber, because a ₹5,000 sensor sitting unsold with a dated shelf life is a real loss. Sensors are temperature-sensitive; keep off the cold-store floor and out of the hill winter.

skuLines.line: Sugar substitutes / diabetic sweeteners
skuLines.examples: Sugar Free Gold pellets & powder, Sugar Free Natura, Sugar Free Green (stevia), Zydus Sugarlite
skuLines.priceBand: ₹75-310 MRP (100 pellets ₹75; 300 pellets ₹206-309; 500 pellets ₹300; 100g Gold/Natura jar ₹154; 200g stevia jar ₹310)
skuLines.marginBand: 18-28% (FMCG-style, no drug licence needed)
skuLines.notes: Sells to a far wider group than actual diabetics — a household with one diabetic switches the whole kitchen. No prescription and no licence issue, so it can also sit on the main POS store shelf, not only in the dispensary. Long shelf life, ideal for a 30-50 km supply run.

skuLines.line: Telmisartan and its FDCs (plain, +HCTZ, +amlodipine, +chlorthalidone, +metoprolol)
skuLines.examples: Telma 20/40/80 (Glenmark), Telma H, Telma AM, Telma CT, Telmikind (Mankind), Truetel 40 (₹106.50/15s)
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 10 / 15 / 30; bottle of 30 for long-term users
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; BP readings and dose changes cluster in cold months (Nov-Feb), when hill winter drives pressures up
skuLines.marginBand: 16% on scheduled strengths; 20-22% on FDCs
skuLines.notes: The single best-selling BP molecule in India — Telma 40 sits in the national top-seller lists. Stock 40mg deepest, then 20 and 80, plus Telma H and Telma AM. Cold weather genuinely raises blood pressure, so a hill campus sees more dose escalations Nov-Feb than a plains store.

skuLines.line: Other ARBs — losartan and olmesartan, plain and +HCTZ / +amlodipine
skuLines.examples: Losar 25/50 (₹158.70/15s), Losacar, Olmesar, Olmetrack, Triolmezest 40 (Sun, ₹323/10s)
skuLines.notes: Keep one alternative ARB family so a patient whose prescriber wrote losartan or olmesartan is not forced onto telmisartan. Depth here is waste; breadth is the point.

skuLines.line: Amlodipine, plain and +atenolol / +bisoprolol
skuLines.examples: Stamlo 5 (Dr Reddy's, ₹80.51/30s), Amlong 5 (Micro, ₹80.51/30s), Amlip 5 (Cipla), Amlopres AT (Cipla, ₹203.92/15s), Amodep AT (FDC), Concor AM 2.5 (Merck)
skuLines.priceBand: ₹19-343 per pack (Amlip 5 10s ₹26.83; Aginal 5 15s ₹40; Stamlo 5 30s ₹80.51; Amlopres AT 30s bottle ₹343.43)
skuLines.marginBand: 16% (amlodipine is scheduled) to 22% on FDCs
skuLines.notes: Cheapest effective BP drug in India — ₹20-40 a month. Ankle swelling is the common complaint that makes patients stop; the pharmacist should flag it rather than let them quietly abandon therapy.

skuLines.line: Beta blockers — metoprolol, atenolol, bisoprolol, carvedilol, nebivolol
skuLines.examples: Metolar / Metolar XR (Cipla), Tenormin / Aten (atenolol), Concor 2.5/5 (Merck), Cardivas 3.125 (₹71.34/15s), Carvistar 3.125 (₹53.85/15s), Nebicard
skuLines.notes: CRITICAL SAFETY LINK TO THE ASTHMA SHELF: non-selective beta blockers can trigger bronchospasm, so an asthmatic on propranolol needs the prescriber flagged. Also never stop abruptly — a stockout here is a rebound-hypertension risk, not just an inconvenience.

skuLines.line: ACE inhibitors — ramipril, enalapril, lisinopril
skuLines.examples: Cardace 2.5/5 (Sanofi, ₹116.63/15s), Ramistar, Envas, Hipril
skuLines.notes: Prescribed heavily where diabetes and BP coexist (kidney protection), which is exactly this staff cohort. The dry cough side-effect gets mistaken for a chest infection and drives inappropriate antibiotic requests — a stewardship link the pharmacist can break.

skuLines.line: Diuretics — chlorthalidone, torsemide, furosemide, spironolactone, HCTZ
skuLines.examples: CTD 6.25/12.5 (₹114.10/15s), Aldactone 25/50 (₹62.66/15s), Dytor 10 (Cipla), Lasix (Sanofi), Tide
skuLines.notes: Aldactone and Dytor also serve cardiac and liver patients. Furosemide is the one line where a same-day supply matters clinically (fluid overload) — hold a small buffer even though it turns slowly.

skuLines.line: Statins — atorvastatin and rosuvastatin, plain and +aspirin/fenofibrate
skuLines.examples: Tonact 10/20 (Lupin, ₹80.05/15s), Lipvas 10/40 (Cipla), Atorva (Zydus), Rosuvas / Rozavel, Ecosprin AV 75/20 & 75/40 (USV), Ecosprin Gold
skuLines.priceBand: ₹34-259 per strip (Lipvas 10 10s ₹53.44; Tonact 10 15s ₹80.05; Ecosprin AV 75/20 15s ₹66.80; Ecosprin Gold 40 15s ₹258.19)
skuLines.marginBand: 16% on scheduled strengths; 20-25% on the AV/Gold capsule combos
skuLines.notes: Atorvastatin 10 and 20 are the volume SKUs. The Ecosprin AV / Gold family is the convenient single-capsule combo an elderly patient actually takes — worth stocking over separate aspirin + statin strips.

skuLines.line: Low-dose aspirin (antiplatelet), 75mg and 150mg
skuLines.examples: Ecosprin 75 (USV, ₹5.29/14s), Ecosprin 150 (₹10.58/14s), Ecosprin 325, Loprin, Delisprin
skuLines.priceBand: ₹5-11 per strip of 14 — one of the cheapest chronic SKUs in India
skuLines.marginBand: 16% (scheduled) — pennies per pack; stock it as a service, not a margin line
skuLines.notes: Ecosprin is India's #1 top-SEARCHED medicine. Absolutely never out of stock: an interrupted antiplatelet in a post-cardiac resident 30-50 km from a hospital is the highest-consequence stockout in this whole list. Enteric-coated, keep dry.

skuLines.line: Clopidogrel, plain and +aspirin
skuLines.examples: Clopilet / Clopilet A 75 (Sun), Deplatt / Deplatt A (Torrent), Plavix, Clopivas AP
skuLines.notes: Post-stent and post-stroke patients. Same never-interrupt logic as aspirin. Flag to the prescriber before any surgical or dental procedure on campus.

skuLines.line: Sublingual nitrate for chest pain (emergency SOS)
skuLines.examples: Sorbitrate 5mg sublingual (Abbott, ₹43.86/50s), Sorbitrate CR 2.6 (₹313.78/30s), Nitro G 2.6, Angised
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 50 sublingual; bottle of 30 CR
skuLines.priceBand: ₹34-44 per strip of 50; ₹180-314 per bottle of 30 CR
skuLines.notes: Cheap, tiny, and the one tablet that buys time during a cardiac event when the nearest hospital is an hour of hill road away. Sublingual nitrate loses potency once the bottle is opened and exposed — date the bottle on opening and rotate. Keep a pack at the dispensary counter AND with the campus first-aid kit.

skuLines.line: Digital upper-arm BP monitor (+ spare cuff, adult and large)
skuLines.examples: Omron HEM-7120 / 7124 / 7156 / 7143T1, Dr Morepen BP-02, Accusure AS, Medtech BP09N
skuLines.packSizes: 1 unit per box; cuffs sold separately
skuLines.seasonality: Sells hardest Nov-Feb and after health camps
skuLines.notes: Prefer upper-arm over wrist — wrist monitors read badly and generate complaints. Stock two price points (a ₹1,500 entry and a ₹2,300 Omron). Batteries are the repeat sale. Hill cold affects LCD and battery life; store above freezing.

skuLines.line: Levothyroxine — the FULL strength ladder, 12.5 to 200 mcg
skuLines.examples: Thyronorm (Abbott) 12.5/25/37.5/50/62.5/75/88/100/112/125/137/150/200mcg, Eltroxin (GSK), Thyrox (Macleods), Thyroford, Thyrofirm, Thyroxinol
skuLines.packSizes: bottle of 30 / 60 / 100 / 120 tablets (bottles, not strips — this is a bottle molecule in India)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round. Hypothyroidism is heavily female-skewed — the married-staff and teaching-staff cohort is the buyer.
skuLines.marginBand: 16% (levothyroxine is a scheduled NLEM formulation — thin, fixed margin)
skuLines.notes: THE DEFINING TEST OF A GOOD CHRONIC SHELF: levothyroxine is dose-titrated in fine steps, so a store that only carries 25/50/100 mcg fails half its patients. Carry the odd strengths (12.5, 37.5, 62.5, 88, 112, 137). Buy the 120s bottle for regulars and the 30s for new starts. Narrow therapeutic index — do NOT casually substitute brands mid-treatment (Thyronorm to Thyrox needs the prescriber's nod). Moisture-sensitive: keep bottles closed and off a damp monsoon floor. Slow-moving odd strengths WILL expire; buy those to the named register only.

skuLines.line: Antithyroid drugs and adjunct for hyperthyroidism
skuLines.examples: Neo Mercazole 5/10 (carbimazole, Abbott), Thyrozol / methimazole, propranolol 10/20/40 (Ciplar) as symptom cover
skuLines.notes: Far lower volume than levothyroxine but there will be a handful of patients, and there is no substitute they can improvise. Carbimazole carries a rare agranulocytosis risk — anyone on it who turns up with a sore throat and fever needs a doctor, not an over-the-counter antibiotic. That is a live stewardship trap in a closed campus.

skuLines.line: Salbutamol reliever inhaler (MDI) and rotacaps
skuLines.examples: Asthalin 100mcg MDI 200md (Cipla, ₹169.88), Levolin 200md MDI (₹291.35), Asthalin 200mcg 60 rotacaps (₹71.77), Aerocort, Levolin 100mcg 30 rotacaps (₹46.06), Asalin
skuLines.packSizes: MDI 120md / 200md canister; box of 30 / 60 rotacaps; tablets 2mg/4mg strip of 45; syrup 100ml
skuLines.priceBand: ₹13-291 (Asthalin MDI ₹169.88; Levolin MDI ₹291.35; Asthalin rotacaps 60s ₹71.77; Asthalin 4mg 45s ₹15.59; Asthalin syrup 100ml ₹18.90)
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp spikes at monsoon onset (Jun-Sep) and again in the cold months (Nov-Feb); spring pollen in the hills (Mar-Apr)
skuLines.marginBand: 16-20% (salbutamol inhalers are NLEM/scheduled)
skuLines.notes: THE most important single SKU in this whole lane for a residential school. Childhood asthma is common, an attack escalates in minutes, and the campus is an hour from a hospital. Hold deep stock of the plain salbutamol MDI, plus the syrup for young children. Pressurised canister: do not let it freeze in a hill winter and never puncture or incinerate. Check the canister count — patients over-use relievers and run empty without noticing.

skuLines.line: Nebuliser respules — levosalbutamol / salbutamol, and ipratropium combination
skuLines.examples: Levolin 0.63mg & 1.25mg respules (Cipla, ₹47-49/pack), Asthalin 2.5mg/2.5ml 5 respules (₹44), Duolin respules (levosalbutamol+ipratropium), Levolin 0.31mg 6s (₹40.38)
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon and winter spikes; wheezy-bronchiolitis season in small children Nov-Feb
skuLines.notes: Unit-dose respules are how you treat a wheezing 3-year-old or a breathless elderly patient who cannot coordinate an inhaler. Cheap, small, fast-moving — hold real depth. Protect from light and freezing. Pair the sale with a nebuliser mask in the right size (infant / child / adult); the wrong mask wastes the drug.

skuLines.line: Inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) controller inhaler and rotacaps
skuLines.examples: Budecort 100/200/400 MDI & rotacaps (Cipla), Flohale (fluticasone, Cipla), Budamate, Ciclohale / ciclesonide
skuLines.seasonality: Prescribed year-round; new starts follow the monsoon and winter flare seasons
skuLines.notes: This is the drug that PREVENTS the emergency. Adherence collapses when a store runs out, because a controller inhaler feels optional to the patient in a good week and they simply stop. A campus store that keeps ICS in stock and reminds refills does more for asthma outcomes here than any other intervention. Rinse-mouth counselling prevents oral thrush.

skuLines.line: ICS + LABA combination inhaler / rotacaps (budesonide-formoterol, fluticasone-salmeterol)
skuLines.examples: Foracort 200/400 MDI & rotacaps (Cipla), Seroflo 100/250/500 MDI & rotacaps (Cipla), Esiflo (Lupin), Budamate, Foracort Forte
skuLines.packSizes: MDI 120md; box of 30 / 60 rotacaps; respules 0.5mg & 1mg 2ml packs of 5
skuLines.priceBand: ₹184-1,042 (Foracort 200mcg 30 rotacaps ₹184.57; Foracort 400 MDI ₹434.70; Seroflo 250 rotacaps 30s ₹591.77; Seroflo 500 MDI ₹1,006.20; Foracort 1mg respules 5s ₹510.70)
skuLines.marginBand: 20-25% (mostly non-scheduled combination brands — the best margin on the respiratory shelf)
skuLines.notes: The mainstay of moderate-to-severe asthma and COPD, and the highest-value respiratory line (₹200-1,000 a device). Standardise on the Cipla family (Foracort/Seroflo) because that is what Indian prescribers write and what the rotahaler devices on campus already accept. Stock the matching Rotahaler device — a rotacap box is useless without one.

skuLines.line: Oral leukotriene antagonist — montelukast, plain and +levocetirizine, adult and paediatric
skuLines.examples: Montair 10 / Montair LC / Montair FX (Cipla), Montek LC (Sun), Montair LC Kid syrup 60ml & chewable, Montecip LC (Cipla GX)
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 10 / 15 tablets; chewable 4mg/5mg strip of 15; syrup 60ml
skuLines.priceBand: ₹75-479 per strip (Montair 10 15s ₹265.22; Montair LC 15s ₹419.79; Montecip LC 10s ₹231.29; Montair LC Kid syrup 60ml ₹158.66; Montair Kid chewable 15s ₹163.95)
skuLines.seasonality: Big monsoon and pollen-season spike; also winter
skuLines.marginBand: 20-25% (non-scheduled; visible price competition means the branded-generic version carries the fatter margin)
skuLines.notes: Montair LC is one of India's top-selling medicines outright. In a residential school the paediatric chewable and the 60ml Kid syrup matter as much as the adult strip — a 7-year-old cannot swallow a 10mg tablet. Montelukast carries a real neuropsychiatric warning (mood, sleep, behaviour) — worth the pharmacist mentioning to hostel wardens dosing children.

skuLines.line: Oral bronchodilator — theophylline / etofylline (+ salbutamol combos)
skuLines.examples: Deriphyllin Retard 150/300 (Zydus, ₹64.43/30s), Dericip Retard 150 (Cipla GX, ₹10.76/10s), Theo Asthalin / Theo Asthalin Forte (Cipla), Deriphyllin syrup 200ml (₹90.06)
skuLines.notes: Older therapy but still widely prescribed in small-town and hill practice, and dirt cheap. Narrow therapeutic window — theophylline toxicity (vomiting, palpitations, seizures) is a genuine risk if a patient doubles up. Keep it, but do not encourage it over inhalers.

skuLines.line: Short-course oral corticosteroid (asthma exacerbation / allergy)
skuLines.examples: Omnacortil 5/10/20/40 (prednisolone, Macleods, ₹7.23-83.57/10s), Omnacortil oral solution 60ml (₹31.39), Wysolone (Pfizer), Medrol (methylprednisolone), Defcort (deflazacort)
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 10; oral solution 30ml / 60ml for children
skuLines.seasonality: Every asthma flare season — monsoon onset and cold snaps
skuLines.notes: A 3-5 day steroid burst is what stops an asthma attack from becoming a hospital transfer. Extremely cheap, so hold a real buffer. Schedule H, prescription-only, and NOT to be handed out casually — repeated unsupervised steroid courses in growing children are harmful. The paediatric oral solution is the SKU most stores forget.

skuLines.line: Intranasal corticosteroid spray (± azelastine) for allergic rhinitis
skuLines.examples: Flomist / Fluticone FT (Cipla), Nasonex (mometasone), Nasivion S, Azeflo (Lupin, ₹576/7ml), Momeflo, Duonase
skuLines.priceBand: ₹275-607 per bottle (Cipla 70md ₹606.55; Azeflo 7ml ₹576; Zydus 6g ₹554.81; Leeford 6g ₹275; Macleods 12ml ₹373.31)
skuLines.seasonality: Strong spring pollen (Mar-Apr) and monsoon dust/damp spikes; the classic hill-station complaint
skuLines.notes: Allergic rhinitis is chronically under-treated and drives the single biggest source of unnecessary antibiotic requests ('constant cold, give me an antibiotic'). Stocking these well is one of the few genuinely effective antibiotic-stewardship moves a retailer can make.

skuLines.line: Oral antihistamines — levocetirizine, cetirizine, fexofenadine, bilastine
skuLines.examples: Levocet / Levorid, Alerid (Cipla), Cetzine (GSK), Allegra 120/180 (Sanofi), Bilagen, Montair BL
skuLines.seasonality: Spring pollen and monsoon peaks; also winter dust in closed hostels
skuLines.marginBand: 22-35% on the branded generics (plain cetirizine is near-commodity)
skuLines.notes: Highest-frequency line in the whole respiratory group and the paediatric syrup is essential for the 5-18 cohort. Cetirizine causes drowsiness — for students in exam season, fexofenadine or bilastine is the better sell. Cheap, long-dated, forgiving stock.

skuLines.line: Spacer / valved holding chamber with paediatric mask
skuLines.examples: Zerostat VT spacer (Cipla, ₹599), Zerostat V, Babyhaler, Rotahaler and Revolizer devices
skuLines.packSizes: 1 unit per box; small / medium / large mask sizes
skuLines.priceBand: ₹499-599 for a spacer; ₹150-300 for a Rotahaler/Revolizer device
skuLines.notes: A child cannot use a bare MDI correctly — without a spacer most of the dose lands in the mouth, and the inhaler 'stops working'. A campus store serving a residential school of 5-18-year-olds must hold spacers and both mask sizes, and someone must be able to DEMONSTRATE the technique. Long shelf life, no licence issue, good margin.

skuLines.line: Nebuliser machine, pulse oximeter and peak-flow meter
skuLines.examples: Omron NE-C106 / NE-C101 compressor nebuliser (₹1,865), Dr Morepen CN-11 (₹1,500), Medtech Handyneb Smart (₹1,843), Breathe O Meter peak-flow (₹564), fingertip pulse oximeters, BPL non-contact IR thermometer (₹3,200)
skuLines.packSizes: 1 unit per box, usually with adult + child mask kit; spare mask kits and tubing sold separately
skuLines.priceBand: Nebuliser ₹1,500-3,430; peak-flow meter ₹564; pulse oximeter ₹700-2,000; IR thermometer ₹1,120-3,200
skuLines.seasonality: Nebulisers sell hardest Nov-Feb and at monsoon onset
skuLines.marginBand: 25-45% on machines; consumables (mask kits, tubing, filters) are the annuity
skuLines.notes: At least two working nebulisers should exist on campus — one for sale/loan and one the dispensary keeps. Spare mask kits and tubing are the forgotten SKU and the reason a machine sits idle. Also stock a loan/rental option: a family will not spend ₹1,800 for one week of a child's bronchiolitis, and the rental keeps the drug sale.

skuLines.line: Amoxicillin and amoxicillin-clavulanate — tablets plus paediatric dry syrup
skuLines.examples: Novaclav 625 (Cipla GX, ₹196.75/10s), Augmentin 625 (GSK), Clavam 625 (Alkem, ₹196.73/10s), Mox 250/500 (Sun), Bactoclav 625 (Micro), Amoxyclav dry syrup 30ml (₹64.68)
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 6 / 10 tablets (a full 5-day course); 30ml / 60ml reconstitutable dry syrup with measuring cap
skuLines.priceBand: ₹92-291 per strip of 10 (625mg); ₹48-179 per dry-syrup bottle
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon (Jun-Sep) and winter (Nov-Feb) respiratory and skin infections
skuLines.marginBand: 16-22% (many strengths are scheduled NLEM formulations)
skuLines.notes: POLICY, NOT JUST STOCK: Schedule H — no sale without a valid prescription from a registered medical practitioner, full stop. On a closed campus the store IS the only source, so lax dispensing here breeds resistance directly in the hostels. Dispense the FULL course as one pack, never a cut strip of 4 tablets — a half course is how resistance is made. Dry syrup for the 5-18 cohort with the measuring cap intact; once reconstituted it keeps only 7 days and must be refrigerated, so counsel that at the counter.

skuLines.line: Azithromycin — 250mg / 500mg short-course packs and paediatric suspension
skuLines.examples: Azee 250/500 (Cipla, ₹126.71/5s), Azicip 500 3s (₹75.53), Azithral (Alembic, ₹125.47/10s), Azincure 500 3s, Azee dry syrup 200mg/5ml
skuLines.packSizes: strip of 3 / 5 / 6 tablets (a complete 3- or 5-day course); 15ml / 30ml suspension
skuLines.marginBand: 20-30% (branded-generic azithromycin carries a wide margin spread — up to 37% visible discounting online)
skuLines.notes: Sold as a complete course by design — the 3-tablet pack IS the treatment, which makes it the easiest antibiotic to dispense responsibly. Schedule H. Over-prescribed for viral fevers in India, so the pharmacist should confirm a prescription exists rather than 'the usual'. Keep both the tablet and the paediatric suspension.

skuLines.line: Oral cephalosporins — cefixime, cefuroxime, cephalexin (+ dry syrups)
skuLines.examples: Zifi 200 (FDC, ₹93.55/10s), Taxim-O 200 (Alkem), Cefaprime 500 (₹238.50/10s), Ceff / Sporidex (cephalexin), Zifi dry syrup 30ml
skuLines.notes: Third-generation cephalosporins fall under SCHEDULE H1 — a separate bound register must record patient name, prescriber, drug and quantity, and be kept THREE YEARS, plus the red-boxed H1 warning on the pack. This register is the single most likely thing a drug inspector will ask for and the most likely thing a campus store gets wrong. Stock a NARROW range (cefixime 200 and one cephalexin) — do not hold high-end cefpodoxime/clav combos as walk-in stock; order those against a named prescription.

skuLines.line: Doxycycline
skuLines.examples: Doxynec (₹52.64/10s), Doxy-1 L-DR (USV), Doxyvac C (₹48.40/10s), Doxt-SL
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon (scrub typhus and leptospirosis are real hill-monsoon risks in Himachal); also long courses for acne in the 15-25 cohort
skuLines.notes: Cheap and clinically important in a wet hill district — undifferentiated monsoon fever is often treated empirically with doxycycline on medical advice. Also the long-course acne drug for teenagers, which makes it a slow-and-steady chronic line, not just acute. Take with water sitting upright; oesophageal irritation is the common complaint.

skuLines.line: Nitrofurantoin (urinary tract infection first-line)
skuLines.examples: Niftas 100 (₹107.91/14s), Nitrofur SR 100 (₹107.91/14s), Nitrobest (₹75.25/10s), Martifur MR
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; rises with reduced fluid intake in cold months
skuLines.notes: UTI is one of the most common reasons a woman on a closed campus needs a same-day antibiotic, and nitrofurantoin is the recommended first-line precisely because it spares the broad-spectrum drugs. Stocking it well is active stewardship. Pair with alkalising sachets (Cital/Alkasol) which need no prescription.

skuLines.line: Metronidazole and ofloxacin-ornidazole combinations (GI and dental)
skuLines.examples: Flagyl / Metrogyl 400 (JB), Olox OZ (₹93.11/10s), Zenflox OZ (Aristo), Normet, O2 (Medley)
skuLines.seasonality: Strong monsoon spike — waterborne GI illness Jun-Sep is the defining seasonal event for a hill campus
skuLines.notes: The monsoon workhorse for amoebic dysentery and giardiasis, and the standard dental-infection cover. Schedule H. Warn hard about alcohol interaction (not an issue in this Sikh institution, but the counselling habit matters) and about the metallic taste that makes patients abandon the course. Always dispense with ORS, not instead of it.

skuLines.line: Fluoroquinolones — levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin (Schedule H1, restricted)
skuLines.examples: Levoflox / Levotas 500 (Torrent), Ciplox 500 (Cipla), Cifran (Sun), Levomac (Macleods)
skuLines.notes: SCHEDULE H1 — separate register, three-year retention, red-boxed warning: 'It is dangerous to take this preparation except in accordance with the medical advice.' Deliberately keep this line SHALLOW: one molecule, one strength, dispensed only against a written prescription and entered in the H1 register the same day. Tendon rupture and nerve damage warnings make these unsuitable for casual use, and they are a priority target of India's antimicrobial-resistance action plan. Never stock reserve orals (linezolid, faropenem, carbapenems) as shelf stock in a campus store.

skuLines.line: Topical antibacterial ointments and creams
skuLines.examples: T-Bact / Bactoderm (mupirocin, GSK/Glenmark), Fucidin (fusidic acid, Leo), Soframycin (framycetin), Neosporin powder, Silverex (silver sulfadiazine)
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon — impetigo, boils and infected insect bites spread fast through hostel dormitories Jun-Sep
skuLines.notes: Bed-to-bed skin infection is a genuine residential-school problem and a topical treats it without a systemic antibiotic — good stewardship and good margin at once. Long shelf life. Mupirocin should still be prescription-governed; do not let it become the shelf remedy for every scratch, because mupirocin resistance follows overuse.

skuLines.line: Anti-epileptics — levetiracetam, valproate, carbamazepine, phenytoin
skuLines.examples: Levipil 250/500/750/1g + Levipil XR + Levipil syrup 100ml (Sun), Levesra 500, Valparin Chrono (Sanofi), Tegretol CR (Novartis), Eptoin (Abbott)
skuLines.notes: Levipil is one of India's top-selling medicines and epilepsy is common enough that a 5,000-person residential campus will have several patients, including children (hence the 100ml syrup). A missed dose can cause a seizure — this is the second most consequence-heavy stockout on this list after insulin and aspirin. Do NOT substitute brands mid-treatment; anti-epileptics are narrow-therapeutic-index drugs where a brand switch can break control. Keep 2-3 months of cover for every named patient.

skuLines.line: Acid suppression — pantoprazole, omeprazole, rabeprazole (+ DSR combos)
skuLines.examples: Pan 40 / Pan D (Alkem, ₹192.80/15s), Pantocid / Pantocid DSR (Sun), Pantosec 40 (Cipla GX, ₹162.84/10s), Omee 20 (Alkem), Nexpro RD 40 (Torrent), Rantac
skuLines.priceBand: ₹75-262 per strip (Pantosec 40 10s ₹162.84; Pan 40 15s ₹192.80; Pantocid DSR 15s ₹252.19; Pantocid 40 15s ₹195.94)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes with exam stress and festival eating
skuLines.marginBand: 20-30% (the branded generics show 47-54% online discounting, so retailer margin here is genuinely wide)
skuLines.notes: Pan 40, Pan D and Omee 20 are among India's most-searched medicines — this is a chronic line whether or not it should be. Many residents self-medicate indefinitely; the pharmacist should push back on years of unsupervised PPI use (B12, magnesium and bone effects). Also the mandatory companion to any NSAID or steroid course.

skuLines.line: Iron + folic acid (and ferrous ascorbate combinations)
skuLines.examples: Orofer XT tablets & syrup (Emcure, ₹635.65/30s bottle), Fericip XT (Cipla, ₹139.11/10s), Autrin, Dexorange syrup, Livogen
skuLines.packSizes: bottle of 30 / strip of 10 / 15; suspension 200ml; paediatric drops 15ml
skuLines.priceBand: ₹75-636 (Orofer XT 30s bottle ₹635.65; Orofer XT 15s ₹349.25; Fericip XT 10s ₹139.11; Orofer XT drops 15ml ₹154.95; 200ml suspension ₹358.95)
skuLines.marginBand: 25-35% (largely non-scheduled nutraceutical-adjacent brands — one of the better margins in this lane)
skuLines.notes: Orofer XT is the #1 top-selling medicine on Indian e-pharmacies. Adolescent-girl anaemia is one of the biggest measurable health burdens in an Indian residential school, and iron is a MONTHS-long chronic course, not a one-off. Carry tablet, syrup AND paediatric drops. Warn about black stools and constipation, which is why patients quit. Take with vitamin C, not with milk or tea.

skuLines.line: Calcium + vitamin D3, and high-dose vitamin D sachets
skuLines.examples: Shelcal 500 / Shelcal XT (Torrent), Cipcal 500 (Cipla), Calcirol 60K sachet (Cadila), Uprise-D3 60K, Depura drops (for infants)
skuLines.packSizes: strip/bottle of 15 / 30 tablets; 60,000 IU sachet (weekly x 8); 400 IU infant drops 15ml
skuLines.priceBand: ₹80-300 per 15-30 tablets; ₹25-40 per 60K sachet; ₹120-200 for infant drops
skuLines.seasonality: Vitamin D demand peaks in winter (Nov-Feb) — short daylight and covered clothing in a cold hill location make deficiency near-universal
skuLines.marginBand: 25-40% (non-scheduled supplements — the highest-margin line in this lane)
skuLines.notes: Genuinely warranted here rather than just a supplement upsell: a cold, high-altitude, largely covered-clothing population with limited winter sun is a textbook vitamin-D-deficient cohort. The weekly 60K sachet course is the standard Indian prescription. Infant drops matter for the married-staff babies. Long shelf life, no cold chain, easy to carry up the hill road.

skuLines.line: ORS and zinc (oral rehydration)
skuLines.examples: Electral powder & ready-to-drink (FDC), Enerzal, Prohance ORS, WHO-formula ORS sachets, Zinconia / Z&D zinc syrup and dispersible tablets
skuLines.packSizes: 21.8g sachet; 200ml/500ml ready-to-drink; zinc 20mg dispersible strip of 10; zinc syrup 60ml
skuLines.priceBand: ₹22-30 per ORS sachet; ₹40-60 ready-to-drink; ₹30-70 per zinc pack
skuLines.seasonality: Heavy monsoon spike (Jun-Sep) plus any hostel GI outbreak; also summer
skuLines.notes: ORS plus zinc is the actual treatment for childhood diarrhoea — the antibiotic usually is not. Stocking ORS deep and dispensing it FIRST is the cheapest antibiotic-stewardship lever a campus store has, and in a monsoon outbreak among 5,000 residents it is the highest-volume item in this whole lane. Use only WHO-formula ORS, not a sugary 'ORS-branded' drink. Feather-light, long-dated, ideal for bulk pre-monsoon stocking before the hill road gets difficult.

trends2026: Generic semaglutide flooded India after the patent expired in March 2026 — 40-50 domestic brands launched (Sun's Sematrinity/Noveltreat, Dr Reddy's Obeda, Zydus's Semaglyn/Alterme/Mashema, Torrent, Glenmark's Glipiq, Eris's Sundae, Natco, Mankind). Live prices: generic oral semaglutide 3mg 10s now ₹881-1,326 against Rybelsus at ₹2,972-3,628. GLP-1s (Rybelsus, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Lirafit) now sit at the TOP of Indian e-pharmacy best-seller lists, and PharmEasy has given 'GLP-1 Medicines' its own top-level navigation category. A chronic shelf that has no GLP-1 in 2026 is missing the fastest-growing therapy in the country.

SGLT2 and DPP-4 triple FDCs have displaced the old metformin-plus-sulfonylurea default as second-line therapy. Live SKUs like Gemer Dapa XR 10/2/500 (three molecules in one tablet), Istamet, Galvus Met, Vysov M and Dapanorm GM mean a store that stocks only metformin and glimepiride now turns away a large share of diabetes prescriptions.

Continuous glucose monitoring has crossed into retail — FreeStyle Libre sensors at ₹4,431-5,138 sit on the same e-pharmacy shelf as ₹800 glucometers. The economics of the diabetes device shelf have shifted from selling meters to selling consumables: strips, lancets, pen needles and now sensors are the annuity.

Q-commerce and e-pharmacy have made a 20-25% discount off MRP the reference price nationwide (every PharmEasy and 1mg listing shows it), and Blinkit/Zepto now run 10-minute pharmacy delivery in metros. Residents of an isolated campus can see that price on their phone even where no one will deliver, so a single-outlet store gets its MRP pricing questioned in a way it did not three years ago.

Antibiotic stewardship enforcement is tightening: Schedule H1 register inspection (patient, prescriber, drug, quantity, kept three years), the red-boxed H1 warning, red-line labelling on prescription-only antibiotic packs, and India's national AMR action plan. For a small store the H1 register — not the stock — is the most likely audit failure.

Molecule-level substitution has gone mainstream: every Indian e-pharmacy result now carries a 'Branded Substitute of the same composition' prompt, and Jan Aushadhi generic pricing anchors what patients think a molecule should cost. Chronic patients increasingly arrive asking for the cheap equivalent by molecule name rather than the brand the doctor wrote.

Chronic-refill subscription programmes (monthly dose packs, refill reminders, auto-renewal against a stored prescription) are now standard practice in Indian organised pharmacy retail and are the main reason chains hold chronic patients against e-pharmacy discounting.

NPPA's annual WPI-linked revision of ceiling prices on the 384 DPCO/NLEM molecules means an entire chronic assortment has to be re-priced every April — telmisartan, metformin, amlodipine, aspirin, levothyroxine, salbutamol and the insulins are all in that price-controlled set.
adjacentServices: Monthly chronic refill register and reminder service — one line per resident (molecule, strength, brand, refill date). On a campus 30-50 km from the nearest market this is the highest-leverage service in the whole category: it converts a stockout from a crisis into a purchase order, and it is how you know whether to buy a ₹5,000 CGM sensor or a bottle of 12.5mcg levothyroxine at all.
Prescription file / repeat-prescription retention, so a resident who has lost their paper can still be served legally, and so the Schedule H and H1 registers are actually defensible at inspection.

Free BP check and a low-cost finger-prick blood sugar counter — footfall driver, drives strip and lancet sales, and catches undiagnosed hypertension and diabetes in a 5,000-person population that has nowhere else to be screened.

Lab sample collection tie-up with a Solan or Chandigarh lab for HbA1c, thyroid profile, lipid profile and CBC — chronic prescriptions cannot be renewed without these, and today the test itself forces a trip off campus.

Teleconsultation link for prescription renewal, so a stable diabetic, hypertensive or thyroid patient does not travel an hour of hill road for a repeat script — and so the store is never asked to dispense a chronic drug without a valid prescription.

Nebuliser and BP-monitor loan or rental instead of purchase — a family will not spend ₹1,800 on a machine for one week of a child's wheeze, and the rental keeps the respule and consumable sale on campus.

Cold storage as a service: a locked, temperature-logged shelf in the pharmacy fridge where residents keep their own insulin pens, which also solves the hill-winter freezing risk in unheated staff quarters.

Inhaler and spacer technique demonstration for school children, hostel wardens and the campus dispensary staff — the difference between an inhaler that works and one the family says has stopped working.
Sharps disposal box service for insulin needles and lancets, collected and destroyed properly rather than going into a campus dustbin used by children.

Pre-monsoon and pre-winter bulk stocking runs with a written buffer list (ORS, respules, relievers, oral steroids, first-line antibiotics), since the hill road is the real constraint on availability, not the supplier.

Expiry management and return-to-stockist arrangement, negotiated up front — without it, the slow-moving odd strengths that make a chronic shelf good (12.5mcg levothyroxine, a spare basal insulin, a ₹5,000 CGM sensor) are exactly what turns into write-off.
